clue.text: Revolutionary paper socialist edited

indicators.note: something revolutionary turns everything over, so the letters before it are thrown into a new order

parts.note: RED is the stock crossword word for a socialist or communist

explanation.surface: A radical newspaper run by a left-winger has been through the editor's hands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' looks like the adjective for the paper, but it signals the anagram of PAPER plus RED.
explanation.definitionFit: A text that has been edited has been made ready for publication, the same sense as a manuscript got ready.

clue.text: Driver in competition placed first after recovery

indicators.note: after puts the placing behind the recovery

parts.note: a rally is a recovery, as in prices or a sports team rallying
1ST, first place, written with I for the figure 1

explanation.surface: A racing driver came first after fighting back.
explanation.definitionFit: A rallyist competes in motor rallies, so drives in competition.

clue.text: Depth in which expert discovered Scottish monster's home

parts.note: a pro is an expert
found means discovered
Loch Ness is the home of the legendary Nessie

explanation.surface: A specialist has located Nessie's lair deep down.
explanation.definitionFit: Profoundness is depth of thought or feeling, the quality of being profound.

clue.text: Groggy after the night before, soldiers may come round now?

definitions.text: Groggy after the night before, soldiers may come round now?

indicators.note: coming round something encloses it, so one piece goes about the others

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps

indicators.note: after puts the groggy part behind the night before

parts.note: eve is the evening before an event
ill means unwell, groggy

explanation.surface: Soldiers feeling rough after a night out may stir only when the bugle sounds.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is the Royal Engineers. 'may come round' signals the container; read whole, the clue pictures bleary troops waking to the bugle, with 'now?' pointing at the moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Reveille is the morning bugle call that wakes soldiers, when they come round from sleep.

clue.text: Lassie's heavenly body?

parts.note: Lassie the collie was a canine film celebrity, and the name of such a celebrity is also that of Sirius, a bright star

explanation.surface: Asking about the star belonging to a Scottish girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lassie' reads as Scots for a girl, but it is the famous film collie.
explanation.definitionFit: Sirius, the brightest star in the night sky, sits in Canis Major and bears this name; Lassie was a canine star too.

clue.text: Restore theatre's appearance

parts.note: rep, short for repertory, is a kind of theatre
an air is an appearance or manner

explanation.surface: Refurbish the look of the playhouse.
explanation.definitionFit: To repair is to restore something broken to good condition.

clue.text: Queen governed island briefly

parts.note: ran means governed or managed
I is the short form of island on maps

explanation.surface: A queen ruled a small island.
explanation.definitionFit: A rani is a Hindu queen or a raja's wife.

clue.text: Crafty, closing window a tiny bit

indicators.note: closing around something shuts it in, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: sly means crafty
a light is a window or pane

explanation.surface: A crafty person shuts a window just a crack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'closing' looks like shutting the window, but it is the container signal: the crafty word wraps around the window.
explanation.definitionFit: Slightly means to a small degree, a little.

clue.text: Finished trip in stretch of turbulent water

parts.note: over means finished, as in 'the game is over'
a trip is a stumble or fall

explanation.surface: Someone completed a journey somewhere with rough water.
explanation.definitionFit: An overfall is a patch of turbulent sea where currents meet or water runs over a shoal.

clue.text: Singer from Scotland making comeback

indicators.note: a comeback goes back the way it came, so the extracted letters are read in reverse
the letters are taken from inside the word Scotland, not from the country

explanation.surface: A Scottish vocalist is returning to the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' lifts OTLA out of the middle of 'Scotland'; 'making comeback' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: An alto is a singer with a low female or high male voice, a voice part in a choir.

clue.text: Liberal seeking election as independent

parts.note: liberal in the sense of free, unrestricted
a candidate who is standing is running for election

explanation.surface: A Liberal Party candidate runs as an independent.
explanation.definitionFit: Something freestanding is self-supporting, needing nothing to hold it up.

clue.text: After first sign of dripping nose, can't get out for a cold remedy

indicators.note: after puts the rearranged letters behind that opening letter
the first sign of a word is its opening letter
out as in out of order, so these letters are muddled

explanation.surface: With a runny nose, you can't go outside, so take a cold cure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can't get out' reads as being stuck indoors, but 'out' is the anagram signal, and its fodder includes 'nose' as well.
explanation.definitionFit: A decongestant is a medicine that clears a blocked nose, taken for colds.

clue.text: Woman educated at length accepts university ceremony

indicators.note: one piece accepting another takes it inside

parts.note: Rita is the heroine of the play and film Educating Rita

explanation.surface: A woman who studied at length goes to a degree ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Educating Rita' is Willy Russell's play about a woman educated as an adult; 'accepts' puts U inside RITA + L.
explanation.definitionFit: A ritual is a formal ceremony with a fixed order of actions.

clue.text: Member of flying troop short of oxygen in atrocious storm

indicators.note: to storm is to rage wildly, so the remaining letters are tossed about
being short of something means lacking it, so one letter is taken away

parts.note: O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A member of a gliding troop runs low on air in terrible weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short of' removes one O from ATROCIOUS, and 'storm' rearranges the remaining ATRCIOUS. 'atrocious' looks like the adjective for the storm, but it is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Air Scouts are a branch of the Scout movement focused on aviation, so one is a member of a flying troop.

clue.text: Having jewellery in ears or nose is deliberate, they say

definitions.text: Having jewellery in ears or nose

indicators.note: what people say is heard, so a word pronounced like studied is wanted

parts.note: a studied action is deliberate, carefully planned

explanation.surface: Piercings of ears or nose are a deliberate choice, people claim.
explanation.definitionFit: Ears or a nose with studs in them are studded, set with small jewels.

clue.text: Expression of impatience after ration cut promptly

indicators.note: after puts the exclamation behind the shortened ration
cut means shortened, losing the last letter

parts.note: a share is a ration or allotted portion
pish is an old exclamation of impatience or contempt

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles impatiently when rations are reduced quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' trims SHARE to SHAR. Sharpish is British informal for quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharpish is informal British for quickly or without delay.

clue.text: Term for a threesome

definitions.meaning: one of the terms of the academic year at older British universities
a set of three people or things

explanation.surface: A word used to describe a group of three.
explanation.walkthrough: Trinity is the name of a university term at Oxford, Cambridge and other old universities, running from spring into summer.
explanation.definitionFit: Trinity term is an academic term, and a trinity is any group of three, as in the Holy Trinity.

clue.text: Perhaps Sun's leader replaced? That's sensible

indicators.note: the leading letter is swapped out for another

parts.note: The Sun is a British daily tabloid, an example of a national newspaper

explanation.surface: Is the Sun getting a new editor? Seems a wise move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader replaced' swaps the N of NATIONAL for R; the clue leaves the new letter for the solver to find. The Sun is a British national newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Rational means based on reason, so sensible.

clue.text: Panel in roof seen in cross-section, from underneath

indicators.note: in a down clue, read from underneath means read upwards, in reverse

parts.note: rood is a cross, as in a church's rood screen, and part means section

explanation.surface: An architect's drawing shows a hatch in the roof.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross-section' looks like a technical drawing, but splits into ROOD and PART; 'from underneath' reverses the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: A trapdoor is a hinged panel set into a floor or ceiling.

clue.text: Directions needed for starters, perhaps

definitions.meaning: starters are one example of the parts of a meal

explanation.surface: Instructions are required for the first part of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Courses are routes taken and also the separate stages of a meal, starters being one.

clue.text: Posh young woman, one rebuffed by a North American citizen

parts.note: gel is a mock-upper-class pronunciation of girl

indicators.note: rebuffed suggests being pushed back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written before being turned round

explanation.surface: A snooty girl is snubbed by someone from North America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rebuffed' turns ONE into ENO. 'North American' reads as one phrase, but North only gives N.
explanation.definitionFit: An Angeleno is a citizen of Los Angeles, so an American city dweller.

clue.text: In state of New York, cannabis commonly attracts strong emotion

indicators.note: commonly means in a common accent, dropping the initial aitch

parts.note: hemp is the cannabis plant
ire is anger, a strong emotion

explanation.surface: In New York, marijuana use stirs up fierce feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'commonly' drops the H of HEMP, as in a Cockney accent.
explanation.definitionFit: New York's nickname is the Empire State, so empire stands for that state.

clue.text: To walk back, you'll need protective covering on shoe

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: back means the word is read in reverse

parts.note: to pace is to walk steadily

explanation.surface: If you walk home, you'll want something to protect your shoes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns PACE into ECAP.
explanation.definitionFit: A toecap is the reinforced cover over the front of a boot or shoe.

clue.text: Faded painting by earliest of Pre-Raphaelites has square picture frame

parts.note: passe means past its best, faded

indicators.note: the earliest of a word is its first letter

parts.note: painting is art
square in the sense of unfashionable, which is also what out means

explanation.surface: A washed-out Pre-Raphaelite picture sits in a square frame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'earliest of' takes P from Pre-Raphaelites, placed by ART. Square and out both mean old-fashioned or not in vogue.
explanation.definitionFit: A passe-partout is a mount or frame for a picture, held together with gummed tape.

clue.text: Beatles' last record, a big hit

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter

parts.note: a log is a record, as in a ship's log

explanation.surface: The Beatles' final record was a huge success.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a slog is a wild, powerful hit.
explanation.definitionFit: A slog is a hard, wild swipe of the ball, as in cricket.

clue.text: Prophet regularly visiting farmhouse

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, taking every other letter

explanation.surface: A prophet makes frequent visits to a farm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the 2nd, 4th, 6th and 8th letters of farmhouse.
explanation.definitionFit: Amos is one of the minor prophets of the Old Testament, with a book named after him.

clue.text: At the end of the day, one might get into Oxford

definitions.text: At the end of the day, one might get into Oxford

parts.words: At the end of the day, one might get into Oxford
parts.note: Oxford is a style of lace-up shoe, and at night a wooden form is pushed into it to keep its shape, not a student entering the university

explanation.surface: Eventually, someone may win a place at Oxford University.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At the end of the day' is the cliché for 'ultimately', but here means literally at night.
explanation.definitionFit: A shoe-shaped wooden or plastic form is put inside shoes overnight to keep them in shape.

clue.text: Thus reworking Trial by Jury, ultimately unique

parts.note: so means thus

indicators.note: reworking something rearranges it, so these letters are reordered
ultimately points to the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: So, revising the Gilbert and Sullivan opera Trial by Jury turns out one of a kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reworking' makes LITAR from TRIAL; 'ultimately' gives Y from Jury.
explanation.definitionFit: Solitary can mean single or sole, the only one, as in a solitary example.
